clipVariesMethod: spine_03 local rotation sampled at 25 evenly-spaced times (0-96% of length) via unreal.AnimationLibrary.get_bone_pose_for_time; variance = sum of per-axis (pitch+yaw+roll) range across samples, degrees. Re-runnable via Scripts/clip_varies_check.py, which reads this manifest's clip list. Supersedes the original 5-sample (0/20/40/60/80%) method used when the clips were first authored: that checker was not committed, and its sampling was too coarse.
clipVariesThresholdRationale: Justified against the measured zero-motion floor (clipVariesFloorDeg, 0.0): 0.5 deg sits roughly midway between that floor and the lowest real clip at 25-sample density (MT_GAS_Idle_Loop, 1.414 deg) -- an order of magnitude clear of float noise. Coded as a hard assertion in Scripts/clip_varies_check.py, not a post-hoc judgment call.
clipVariesFloorMethod: Two measured negative controls, same instrument (get_bone_pose_for_time), not inferred: (a) MT_GAS_Idle_Loop/spine_03 resampled at one fixed time value (t=5.0s) x5 -> 0.0 deg exactly, proving the instrument's own zero; (b) every clip's translation channel on the same probe bone (spine_03 is rigid-parented, so its local translation is static regardless of animation content) -> 0.0 deg on all 8 clips, i.e. a genuinely static reference read by the same code path as the rotation numbers.
clipVariesWindowNote: minWindowVarianceDeg = minimum rot variance across any consecutive 5-sample window (of the 25) -- catches a mid-clip freeze that whole-clip variance would average away against motion elsewhere. Reported per clip below, not gated (a real clip can legitimately hold a near-still pose for part of its length; see MT_GAS_Gesture_B).

clips.spotCheckNote: Auto-triggered: 1.414 deg is below the 2.0 deg near-low cutoff. Arm/hand bones show comparable-or-larger variance than spine_03, consistent with idle breathing/sway also reaching the arms. Not the clip flagged as weakest (MT_GAS_Gesture_B), but caught by the same general rule.

The weakest data point under the original 5-sample method (1.386 deg). Denser 25-sample spine_03 already raised it to 3.347 deg (above the 0.5 threshold and the 2.0 near-low cutoff), and the hand/arm spot-check confirms why it read low: spine_03 legitimately under-reports this clip -- the animation lives in the arms/hands (a bench-sit interaction), which read 8-9x larger than the spine. minWindowVarianceDeg=0.09681 shows a genuinely near-still ~5s window mid-clip (a held pose while seated); that is real content, not a bake defect, corroborated by both the whole-clip spine reading and the large hand-bone variance. Not downgraded.
